title: Shader Frequency Visualizer: Avocado & BoomBox
description: A BoomBox emits visible sound waves rendered with custom shaders that dynamically distort and recolor a nearby Avocado. The user adjusts frequency, amplitude, distortion mode, color palette, wave shape, and blend factor through a control panel, watching the Avocado morph and pulse in real-time as the shader parameters change.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads both shared_assets/Avocado.glb and shared_assets/BoomBox.glb using GLTFLoader. Place the BoomBox on the left side of the scene at (-1.5, 0, 0) scaled to 80x and the Avocado on the right at (1.5, 0, 0) scaled to 30x. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 1.5, 4) looking at the origin with OrbitControls enabled. Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (3, 5, 2) with intensity 1.2. Create visible sound wave rings between the two objects using a custom ShaderMaterial on torus geometries that animate outward from the BoomBox toward the Avocado, with a vertex shader that oscillates vertices based on a time uniform. Apply a custom ShaderMaterial to the Avocado model by traversing its meshes and replacing their materials. The Avocado's vertex shader should displace vertices along their normals using a sine-based distortion controlled by frequency and amplitude uniforms. The fragment shader should blend the original texture color with a procedural color palette using a mix factor uniform, and apply a pulsing glow effect. Build an HTML/CSS control panel (top-right, semi-transparent dark background) with these six labeled inputs: (1) a slider for Frequency (range 1.0-20.0, default 5.0, step 0.5), (2) a slider for Amplitude (range 0.0-0.5, default 0.1, step 0.01), (3) a dropdown for Distortion Mode with options Sine, Sawtooth, and Square that changes the displacement function in the shader, (4) a dropdown for Color Palette with options Neon, Warm, and Cool that shifts the procedural color in the fragment shader, (5) a slider for Wave Shape controlling the ring geometry tube radius (0.005-0.05, default 0.02), (6) a slider for Blend Factor (0.0-1.0, default 0.5, step 0.05) controlling how much procedural color overrides the original texture. Each input change must update the corresponding shader uniform or geometry parameter immediately. Animate everything in a requestAnimationFrame loop, advancing a time uniform for continuous wave motion and Avocado pulsing. Ensure the scene renders correctly with proper disposal of old geometries when Wave Shape changes.
